summary: This nginx configuration sets up a web server for a Docusaurus documentation site with HTTPS support. It redirects all unencrypted HTTP traffic to HTTPS, serves the site's files from a specific directory, handles client-side routing by falling back to index.html, and optimizes caching for static assets like images and fonts.

explanations.8: The $host and $request_uri are variables that nginx automatically fills in—$host is the domain name the user visited, and $request_uri is everything after the domain (the path and query string), so this preserves exactly what the user was trying to access when redirecting to HTTPS.
explanations.13: This tells nginx to accept both regular HTTPS connections (443 ssl) and the faster HTTP/2 protocol on the same port, which modern browsers prefer.
explanations.28: TLSv1.2 and TLSv1.3 are the secure encryption protocols that browsers use to talk to the server; older versions like TLS 1.0 are disabled because they're no longer considered safe.
explanations.30: This picks strong encryption ciphers (HIGH) and explicitly excludes weak ones (aNULL and MD5), ensuring the connection uses secure mathematical algorithms.
explanations.40: $uri is the file path the user requested; this line says 'try to serve that exact file, then try it as a folder, and if neither exists, serve index.html instead'—this is how single-page apps like Docusaurus handle routing in the browser.
explanations.44: The ~* means 'match these file extensions case-insensitively'; this rule targets all common static files like stylesheets, scripts, images, and fonts.
explanations.45: Setting expires to 1 year tells browsers to cache these files locally for a very long time, so they don't need to download them again when revisiting the site.
